description: Canonical pulled-quotes from the Mayhew extract — verbatim text, speaker attribution, dialect_level, and a TTS-normalised rendition suitable for narration engines that struggle with 19th-century dialect spellings. Not exhaustive; curated for the most iconic, emotionally-loaded, or game-useful lines. For full testimony, load the corresponding character file.

dialect_levels.moderate: Some period markers (elisions, archaic forms) but mostly readable.
dialect_levels.heavy: Phonetic spellings preserved by Mayhew (v/w swap, dropped consonants, cant vocabulary). Use TTS-normalised version for voice engines.

entries.text: The reason I likes this sort of life is, 'cause I can sit down when I likes, and nobody can't order me about.
entries.tts_normalized: The reason I like this sort of life is because I can sit down when I like, and nobody can order me about.
entries.context: The tosher's own summary of his trade's appeal — the headline line for the shore-worker's ethic of autonomy.

entries.text: I've worked Cuckold's P'int for more nor twenty year.
entries.tts_normalized: I've worked Cuckold's Point for more than twenty years.
entries.context: The tosher's territorial signature — Cuckold's Point is his beat, his identity, and his twenty-year trade.

entries.text: Them there water rats, too, is far more ferociouser than any other rats, and they'd think nothink of tackling a man, if they found they couldn't get away no how.
entries.tts_normalized: Those water rats are far more ferocious than any other rats, and they'd think nothing of tackling a man if they found they couldn't get away.
entries.context: The central hazard of the trade — cornered water-rats in the sewers. Preceded directly by the rat-eaten corpse anecdote.

entries.text: A cove can't stop in longer than six or seven hour, 'cause of the tide; you must be out before that's up.
entries.tts_normalized: A man can't stop in longer than six or seven hours, because of the tide — you must be out before that's up.
entries.context: The trade's hard constraint — the Thames tidal cycle caps every descent. Six hours is the working window.

entries.text: I know a place now where there's more than two or three hundred weight of metal all rusted together, and plenty of money among it too; but it's too heavy to carry it out, so it 'ill stop there I s'pose till the world comes to an end.
entries.tts_normalized: I know a place now where there's more than two or three hundredweight of metal all rusted together, and plenty of money among it too — but it's too heavy to carry it out, so it'll stop there I suppose till the world comes to an end.
entries.context: The tosher's unresolved treasure hook — two or three hundredweight of rusted metal too heavy to extract. A ready-made quest seed.

entries.text: I only wish I'd back all the money I've guv to the publican, and I wouldn't care how the wind blew for the rest of my life.
entries.tts_normalized: I only wish I had back all the money I've given to the publican, and I wouldn't care how the wind blew for the rest of my life.
entries.context: The trade's hidden reality — the big hauls ran straight to the pub. Spoken immediately after he describes finding £2 each for a day's work.

entries.text: When we comes to a narrow-place as we don't know, we takes the candle out of the lantern and fastens it on the hend of the o, and then runs it up the sewer, and if the light stays in, we knows as there a'n't no danger.
entries.tts_normalized: When we come to a narrow place we don't know, we take the candle out of the lantern and fasten it on the end of the hoe, and then run it up the sewer — and if the light stays in, we know there isn't any danger.
entries.context: The foul-air test. Canary-in-a-mine logic, trade-craft preserved verbatim.

entries.text: Father vos a dustie;—vos at it all his life, and grandfather afore him for I can't tell how long.
entries.tts_normalized: Father was a dustman — was at it all his life, and grandfather before him for I can't tell how long.
entries.context: The dustman's opening self-description — the v/w swap identifies the accent in two words. Hereditary trade.

entries.text: I don't know what it's good for. It may be wery well for the likes o' you, but I doesn't know it 'u'd do a dustie any good.
entries.tts_normalized: I don't know what it's good for. It may be very well for the likes of you, but I don't know it would do a dustman any good.
entries.context: On schooling — class-cleaving judgment of book-learning as not for his kind.

entries.text: No, we ain't married 'zactly, though it's all one for all that. I sticks to Sall, and Sall sticks to I, and there's an end on't:—vot is it to any von?
entries.tts_normalized: No, we ain't married exactly, though it's all one for all that. I stick to Sall, and Sall sticks to me, and there's an end of it — what is it to anyone?
entries.context: The dustman on his common-law partner Sall. One of the tender moments in the extract.

entries.text: Two or three pipes o' baccer, and a pot or two of good heavy and a song, and then I tumbles in with my Sall, and I'm as happy as here and there von.
entries.tts_normalized: Two or three pipes of tobacco, and a pot or two of good heavy and a song, and then I tumble in with my Sall, and I'm as happy as here and there one.
entries.context: The dustman's catalogue of pleasures — pipe, beer, song, bed. A complete contentment aesthetic in one sentence. 'Heavy' = porter (strong dark beer).

entries.text: I could never bear the thought of going into the 'great house' [workhouse].
entries.tts_normalized: I could never bear the thought of going into the great house — the workhouse.
entries.context: The widow's absolute line — she will starve on dogs' dung before entering the workhouse. Mayhew's annotation [workhouse] preserved.

entries.text: He had got intoxicated while the ship was lying in harbour, and, going down the side to get into a bumboat, and buy more drink, he had fallen overboard and was drowned.
entries.tts_normalized: He had got intoxicated while the ship was lying in harbour, and, going down the side to get into a bumboat and buy more drink, he had fallen overboard and was drowned.
entries.context: The widow narrates her first husband's death from the Neptune East Indiaman in Bombay harbour — fully literary register.

entries.text: I had eight children at one time, and there is not one of them alive now.
entries.tts_normalized: I had eight children at one time, and there is not one of them alive now.
entries.context: Single-line register of accumulated Victorian working-class mortality. Her daughter was the last, who died at 30 in childbirth.

entries.text: It is very cold in winter to stand in the mud without shoes.
entries.tts_normalized: It is very cold in winter to stand in the mud without shoes.
entries.context: The 9-year-old's single direct quote on the physical experience of the trade. He adds that he does not mind it in summer.

entries.text: God was God. He had heard he was good, but didn't know what good he was to him.
entries.tts_normalized: God was God. He had heard he was good, but didn't know what good he was to him.
entries.context: Mayhew's paraphrase of the boy's theology. One of the most-quoted lines from the entire volume — a working-class child's unsentimental rebuttal of evangelical certainty.

entries.text: London was England, and England, he said, was in London, but he couldn't tell in what part.
entries.tts_normalized: London was England, and England, he said, was in London — but he couldn't tell in what part.
entries.context: The mud-lark's working geography — no notion of anything outside his immediate parish. A single-sentence geography lesson in Victorian deprivation.

entries.text: It would be a waste of time to inquire for them by their right names, even if you were acquainted with them, for none else would know them… while under the title of Lanky Bill, Long Tom, One-eyed George, Short-armed Jack, they are known to every one.
entries.tts_normalized: It would be a waste of time to inquire for them by their right names, even if you were acquainted with them, for none else would know them — while under the title of Lanky Bill, Long Tom, One-eyed George, Short-armed Jack, they are known to every one.
entries.context: Mayhew's own framing at the start of the tosher chapter — the cohort nicknames, ready-made NPC roster.

entries.text: I yarns about half-a-bull [2s. 6d.] a day, take one day with another.
entries.tts_normalized: I earn about half-a-bull — two shillings sixpence — a day, taking one day with another.
entries.context: The dustman's daily wage, with Mayhew's editorial gloss of the slang into standard currency. 'Half-a-bull' = 2s 6d = modern ≈£19 (BoE CPI 1851→2024).

entries.text: There's tventy on us vorks here—riglar. I don't think there's von on 'em 'cept Scratchey Jack can read, but he can do it stunning; he's out vith the cart now, but he's the chap as can patter to you as long as he likes.
entries.tts_normalized: There's twenty of us works here — regular. I don't think there's one of them except Scratchey Jack can read — but he can do it stunning. He's out with the cart now, but he's the chap as can patter to you as long as he likes.
entries.context: One literate man in twenty dustmen. Useful as a literacy-rate anchor for any sociological or game-systems model.

entries.text: I was yesterday out all day, and went round Aldgate, Whitechapel, St. George's East, Stepney, Bow, and Bromley, and then came home; after that, I went over to Bermondsey, and there I got only 6d. for my pains.
entries.tts_normalized: I was yesterday out all day, and went round Aldgate, Whitechapel, St George's East, Stepney, Bow, and Bromley, and then came home; after that, I went over to Bermondsey, and there I got only sixpence for my pains.
entries.context: Eastside–Southside walking beat, 10+ miles, one sixpence. A ready-made game route or interactive-walkthrough tour spine.
